clue.text: Complaint resulting from a character-forming occupation

definitions.text: Complaint resulting from a character-forming occupation

parts.words: Complaint resulting from a character-forming occupation
parts.note: surface reading: an ailment caused by a job that shapes someone's personality; setter's reading: a job forming characters, that is, letters of the alphabet with a pen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Character-forming' suggests building moral fibre, as in a tough job; here the characters are letters written by hand all day.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful cramp of the hand muscles is the classic ailment of people who write by hand for long hours.

clue.text: Evidence provided by joker on loch

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting above, so the first piece is placed over the second

parts.note: a wit is someone who makes jokes
Loch Ness, the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Testimony offered by a prankster about Scotland's famous loch.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness is to give testimony, so the word stands for evidence offered in court.

clue.text: Senselessness of one girl brought up in New York

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in places the girl's name within the city's abbreviation

parts.note: the standard abbreviation

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl raised in New York is accused of foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanity is silly, empty pointlessness, a lack of meaning or sense.

clue.text: Coming out east, replacing youth leader in major crisis

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the word counts

parts.note: the first letter of youth
an emergency is a serious crisis

explanation.surface: An Eastern figure emerging and taking over from a young leader amid a national crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The final Y of the crisis word is swapped for E, the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergence is the act of appearing or coming out into view from hiding.

clue.text: Fires in containers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dismisses from a job
second meaning: large bags of coarse cloth

explanation.surface: Blazes breaking out inside storage bins.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means dismissing an employee, and the plural noun names big bags for coal or potatoes.

clue.text: Become entangled in fortification

parts.note: to ravel is to become tangled up
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone getting caught up in the defences of a fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like the link to the definition, but it supplies the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ravelin is an outwork of a fort, a V-shaped detached bastion built in front of the main wall.

clue.text: Political theory of the big brotherhood ?

parts.words: Political theory of the big brotherhood ?
parts.note: surface reading: an ideology of a large fraternity, or of Big Brother's world; setter's reading: the most famous set of comic brothers, the film comedians Groucho, Harpo and Chico

explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Brother' evokes Orwell's totalitarian state; the real brothers are the Hollywood comedy team sharing a surname with the philosopher Karl.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the economic and political doctrine of Karl Marx, centred on class struggle and common ownership.

clue.text: One winter she cracked up, knowing no more than before

indicators.note: something cracked up has broken into pieces and been reassembled differently

parts.note: the fodder, all twelve letters used

explanation.surface: A woman had a breakdown one winter and came out of it none the wiser.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone left as ignorant after an explanation or experience as they were at the start.

clue.text: Features behind old hat and beard?

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the features are placed following the other piece

parts.note: old hat means out of fashion, or simply out
the features together make up the face

explanation.surface: A description of a face hidden behind an old hat and a bushy beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places the features after old hat. 'Beard' looks like a noun about facial hair but is the verb meaning to confront boldly.
explanation.definitionFit: To beard someone is to defy them openly, which is what staring down an opponent does.

clue.text: Concealment of deliveries in vessel

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second, which wraps around it

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries from one bowler

explanation.surface: A shipment hidden away inside a container.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six balls bowled in a row, so 'deliveries' are bowled balls, not parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover-up is an attempt to hide the truth about wrongdoing, a deliberate concealment.

clue.text: Where reporters insist on proof, royalty initially being involved

parts.note: to press is to insist or urge

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside, so the letter is set within the proof

parts.note: a galley proof is a printer's trial copy

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of royalty

explanation.surface: Journalists demanding evidence of royal involvement in a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: A galley is a proof run off from typeset text before the pages are made up.
explanation.definitionFit: The press gallery is the area in a parliament or court set aside for journalists to watch proceedings.

clue.text: It's late in the day for smoothing things out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the time after afternoon and before night
second meaning: making level, from the verb to even

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that it is rather late to be patching up a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a whole phrase standing for the noun; 'late in the day' usually means too late to help.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the closing part of the day, while the verb form describes levelling a surface flat.

clue.text: Ordinary student in burlesque

indicators.note: in puts the student inside the word for burlesque

parts.note: burlesque is mocking parody, a form of satire
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An average student taking part in a comic stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinary' looks like an adjective but is a heraldry noun: an ordinary is one of the simple bold shapes on a shield, such as the diagonal cross.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a saltire, the diagonal St Andrew's cross, is one of the basic charges called ordinaries.

clue.text: Dog seen in river in the borders of Hungary

indicators.note: in puts the river inside the letters taken from the country
borders are the edges, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the country's name
the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: A dog spotted swimming in a river near the Hungarian frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky is a sturdy Arctic sled dog with a thick coat.

clue.text: Sobriquets for Parkhurst and the Scrubs?

definitions.text: Sobriquets for Parkhurst and the Scrubs?

parts.words: Sobriquets for Parkhurst and the Scrubs?
parts.note: surface reading: informal names given to two particular places or people; setter's reading: these are prisons, and a prison is a nick in British slang, so the names are names of nicks

explanation.walkthrough: Parkhurst is a prison on the Isle of Wight and the Scrubs is Wormwood Scrubs in London; 'nick' is British slang for a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobriquets are affectionate or informal alternative names, which is what this compound word ordinarily means.

clue.text: Isolated in pass — extremely chancy position for a soldier

indicators.note: in places the isolated word inside the mountain pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
lone means solitary, isolated

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of chancy

explanation.surface: A soldier cut off in a mountain pass finds himself in a very risky position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position' looks like a battlefield spot but is a rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonelcy is the rank or office held by a colonel, an army post high in the officer ranks.

clue.text: Breakfast, say, consisting entirely of this bread

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective for this kind of bread, read here as the bread itself

parts.note: entirely means completely, as a whole
breakfast is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone describes a breakfast made up only of brown bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consisting' links the parts: a meal that is entire. 'say' marks breakfast as just one example of the word needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal bread is baked from flour milled from the entire wheat grain, bran included.

clue.text: Girl imbibing popular mineral

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the girl's name takes the other word inside it

parts.note: a girl's name
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A girl drinking a well-liked mineral water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mineral' suggests mineral water to go with 'imbibing'; it is the rock-forming kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is an olive-green silicate rock-forming mineral, common in basalt and gem-quality as peridot.

clue.text: Like tasty food for eastern leaders on board

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting above, so these letters go over the next piece
leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letters of the word are wanted

parts.note: the two leading letters of eastern
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Choosing palatable food for oriental rulers sitting round a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is eatable is fit to be eaten, as tasty food plainly is.

clue.text: Firm in Colombia introducing a drink

indicators.note: introducing means coming before, so these parts lead in front of the final letter

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
CO is the international country code for Colombia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company in Colombia bringing a beverage to market.
explanation.walkthrough: Colombia suggests coffee, a natural false path; the drink is the hot chocolate one instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot beverage made from powdered cacao beans mixed with milk or water.

clue.text: A military expedition is unprepared without it

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the first word is wrapped around the second

parts.note: crude means raw, unrefined, unprepared
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A warning that an army campaign will be caught unready without some missing element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but it means outside. 'It' is old slang for sex appeal, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crusades were medieval military campaigns to the Holy Land, so a crusade is such an expedition.

clue.text: A small circle headed by the nobility

definitions.text: A small circle headed by the nobility

parts.words: A small circle headed by the nobility
parts.note: surface reading: an exclusive little social group led by aristocrats; setter's reading: a small ring worn on the heads of noblemen, a lesser crown

explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle' suggests a clique and 'headed by' its leaders; the circle is a band of metal and the heads are literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by peers and peeresses, whose design shows their rank.

clue.text: Partners about to attack old cheese

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the partners go round the other pieces

parts.note: South and North are partners at the bridge table
to tilt at someone is to attack, as a jousting knight charges
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A couple are about to tuck into some cheese that has gone past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, and North sits partnered with South.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a famous English blue cheese, originally sold in the village of that name.

clue.text: Post providing security in mid-flight

parts.note: surface reading: a job guarding an aircraft during its journey, like an air marshal; setter's reading: a flight of stairs, where a sturdy upright supports the handrail

explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' and 'security' suggest a guard's job on a plane; the flight is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the central pillar of a spiral stair, or the upright at a landing that anchors the banister.

clue.text: In which a road user makes no progress

definitions.text: In which a road user makes no progress

parts.words: In which a road user makes no progress
parts.note: surface reading: a place or situation, like a traffic jam, where drivers are stuck; setter's reading: the gear position where the engine turns but the car does not move

explanation.walkthrough: 'In which' suggests a place such as a jam or a queue; it is the gearbox setting a driver is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: In a car's gearbox, this position disconnects the engine from the wheels, so the vehicle stays where it is.

clue.text: Sort of trout — a brown one, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a species of trout with a pinkish stripe along its side
second meaning: in the Guide movement this is the youngest section, whose members may later move up to become Brownies

explanation.walkthrough: The brown trout is a species too, so the second half seems to repeat the first. Here a 'brown one' is a Brownie, and members of the youngest Guide section often go on to join the Brownies.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow trout is a common game and farmed fish; the Guide section for the youngest girls bears the same name.

clue.text: Trainee wage slave on the line

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the worker follows the abbreviation here

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
a wage slave is someone who works to earn a living

explanation.surface: A trainee is a drudge working on the production line.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone being taught a skill, such as a learner driver, is a trainee still acquiring it.

clue.text: Ruddy job many left, being sent to other posts

parts.note: ruddy means reddish in colour

indicators.note: left here means departed, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: a job is a form of employment
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: A wretched job that many people quit as they were moved elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like an anagram signal or a direction, but it means departed: the M for many walks out of the job word.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeployment is the reassignment of staff or troops to different roles or places.
